facts.text: A space-filling design spreads test points as evenly as possible across the ranges of several continuous parameters at once so that no region of the space is left unexplored.
facts.quote: A space-filling design spreads test points as evenly as possible across the ranges of several continuous parameters at once, so that no region of the space is left unexplored.

facts.text: Latin hypercube is the best-known example of a space-filling design.
facts.quote: The Latin hypercube is the best-known example.

facts.text: A Latin hypercube design divides each parameter's range into n equal slices and places n points so that every slice of every parameter is used exactly once.
facts.quote: Each parameter's range is cut into n equal slices, and the design places n points so that every slice of every parameter is used exactly once

facts.text: Sobol sequences and other quasi-random designs achieve an even spread of test points similar to Latin hypercube designs, but in a different way.
facts.quote: Sobol sequences and other quasi-random designs achieve a similar even spread in a different way.

facts.text: Space-filling designs cover continuous parameters more evenly than naive random draws.
facts.quote: these designs cover continuous parameters more evenly than naive random draws

facts.text: Space-filling designs are useful for exploration and for training surrogate models, which are fast approximate models of a simulator's response.
facts.quote: are useful for exploration and for training surrogate models, which are fast approximate models of the simulator's response [Chapter 9].

facts.text: Even parameter-space coverage does not represent operational probability: a uniformly covered parameter box does not represent real quarry traffic, where most approaches are slow and most weather is clear.
facts.quote: A uniformly covered box of parameters is not a picture of a real quarry's traffic, where most approaches are slow and most weather is clear.

facts.text: Space-filling designs treat unrealistic parameter regions exactly like realistic regions unless constraints and distributions are added.
facts.quote: Space-filling designs treat unrealistic regions exactly like realistic ones unless constraints and distributions are added.

facts.text: Space-filling designs can support a claim of even geometric spread through the chosen region, but cannot support claims about rates, worst cases or operational frequency.
facts.quote: So they can claim "even geometric spread through the chosen region" and cannot claim rates, worst cases or operational frequency [Chapter 9].

facts.text: The booklet places space-filling designs alongside combinatorial designs in the coverage stream, never as a basis for the release claim.
facts.quote: The booklet puts space-filling designs in the coverage stream alongside combinatorial designs: good for understanding how detection range varies with dust, glare and speed, and for feeding surrogate-guided search, but never for the release claim [Chapter 9].
